paragraphs.text: For most of the twentieth century, companies judged their employees mainly by output: how many products they made or how many sales they achieved. Only in recent decades have large employers begun to measure how staff feel about their work, often through short online surveys sent every few weeks.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Supporters of these surveys point to a clear link between wellbeing and performance. A study of 1,800 call-centre workers found that in weeks when employees reported being happier, they made more calls per hour and converted more of those calls into sales. The effect was strongest among newer staff.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Critics argue that the surveys themselves can cause harm. If workers suspect that their answers are not anonymous, they may give the responses they think managers want, making the results useless. In one company, scores rose sharply after a manager publicly praised the teams with the highest ratings.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: There is also disagreement about what should be measured. Some surveys ask simply whether people are satisfied, while others ask about specific experiences, such as whether they feel their opinions are heard or whether they have the equipment they need. Researchers generally find the second kind more useful, because the answers suggest what could be changed.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Measuring wellbeing is pointless unless something happens as a result. Employees who complete surveys repeatedly without seeing any response often become more cynical than those who were never asked. For this reason, several consultants recommend that companies share the results with staff and announce at least one change after each survey.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: Smaller businesses rarely use formal surveys, relying instead on regular conversations between managers and staff. A recent report suggested that this informal approach can be just as effective, provided managers are trained to listen rather than to defend decisions already made.
paragraphs.label: F

items.quote: they may give the responses they think managers want
items.prompt: a warning that workers may not answer honestly

explanation.en: If answers are not anonymous, workers “may give the responses they think managers want” → C. “Not answer honestly” paraphrases this.
explanation.kk: Жауаптар жасырын болмаса, қызметкерлер «may give the responses they think managers want» → C. «Not answer honestly» осының басқаша айтылымы.
explanation.ru: Если ответы не анонимны, работники «may give the responses they think managers want» → C. «Not answer honestly» пересказывает это.

items.quote: companies judged their employees mainly by output
items.prompt: a description of how employees used to be judged

explanation.en: How staff used to be judged is at the start of paragraph A: “For most of the twentieth century, companies judged their employees mainly by output” → A.
explanation.kk: Қызметкерлерді бұрын қалай бағалағаны — A абзацының басында: «For most of the twentieth century, companies judged their employees mainly by output» → A.
explanation.ru: Как раньше оценивали сотрудников — в начале абзаца A: «For most of the twentieth century, companies judged their employees mainly by output» → A.

items.quote: The effect was strongest among newer staff.
items.prompt: the finding that one group benefited more than others

explanation.en: “The effect was strongest among newer staff” — newer staff gained most → B.
explanation.kk: «The effect was strongest among newer staff» — жаңа қызметкерлерге әсері бәрінен күшті болған → B.
explanation.ru: «The effect was strongest among newer staff» — новые сотрудники выиграли больше других → B.

items.quote: several consultants recommend that companies share the results with staff and announce at least one change after each survey
items.prompt: advice about what employers should do after each survey

explanation.en: The consultants’ advice is to share results and “announce at least one change after each survey”. That is what to do after a survey → E.
explanation.kk: Консультанттардың ұсынысы: нәтижені бөлісу және «announce at least one change after each survey». Бұл сауалнамадан кейін не істеу керегі → E.
explanation.ru: Совет консультантов: делиться результатами и «announce at least one change after each survey». Это рекомендация, что делать после опроса → E.

items.quote: Some surveys ask simply whether people are satisfied, while others ask about specific experiences
items.prompt: a comparison of two kinds of survey question

explanation.en: Two kinds of question: general (“whether people are satisfied”) and about “specific experiences”, with the second found more useful → D.
explanation.kk: Сұрақтың екі түрі: жалпы («whether people are satisfied») және нақты тәжірибе туралы («specific experiences»), екіншісі пайдалырақ деп саналады → D.
explanation.ru: Два вида вопросов: общий («whether people are satisfied») и о конкретном опыте («specific experiences»), и второй признан полезнее → D.

items.quote: relying instead on regular conversations between managers and staff
items.prompt: a method some employers use instead of surveys

explanation.en: Small businesses skip surveys, “relying instead on regular conversations between managers and staff” → F.
explanation.kk: Шағын бизнес сауалнамасыз, «relying instead on regular conversations between managers and staff» → F.
explanation.ru: Малый бизнес обходится без опросов, «relying instead on regular conversations between managers and staff» → F.

items.quote: scores rose sharply after a manager publicly praised the teams with the highest ratings
items.prompt: an example of a manager’s behaviour affecting survey results

explanation.en: “scores rose sharply after a manager publicly praised the teams with the highest ratings” → C. C for the second time — allowed by the NB.
explanation.kk: «scores rose sharply after a manager publicly praised the teams with the highest ratings» → C. C әрпі екінші рет — NB бұған рұқсат береді.
explanation.ru: «scores rose sharply after a manager publicly praised the teams with the highest ratings» → C. Буква C второй раз — это допускает NB.

items.quote: often through short online surveys sent every few weeks
items.prompt: a reference to how often surveys are usually sent

explanation.en: “short online surveys sent every few weeks” — how often they are sent → A. Paragraph E mentions repeated surveys but gives no frequency.
explanation.kk: «short online surveys sent every few weeks» — сауалнама жіберу жиілігі → A. E абзацы қайталанатын сауалнама туралы, бірақ жиілігін атамайды.
explanation.ru: «short online surveys sent every few weeks» — частота рассылки опросов → A. Абзац E говорит о повторных опросах, но частоту не называет.

items.quote: Employees who complete surveys repeatedly without seeing any response often become more cynical
items.prompt: the negative effect of asking for opinions and then ignoring them

explanation.en: Employees who fill in surveys and see no response “often become more cynical than those who were never asked”. That is the harm of asking and ignoring → E.
explanation.kk: Қызметкерлер сауалнама толтырып, ешқандай жауап көрмесе, «often become more cynical than those who were never asked». Бұл жауапсыз қалған сұрақтың зияны → E.
explanation.ru: Если работники заполняют опросы и не видят реакции, они «often become more cynical than those who were never asked». Это вред от вопросов без ответа → E.

items.quote: provided managers are trained to listen rather than to defend decisions already made
items.prompt: a condition for an informal approach to work well

explanation.en: The informal approach works “provided managers are trained to listen” → F. “Provided” introduces the condition.
explanation.kk: Бейресми тәсіл «provided managers are trained to listen» болса ғана нәтиже береді → F. «Provided» шартты білдіреді.
explanation.ru: Неформальный подход работает, «provided managers are trained to listen» → F. «Provided» вводит условие.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–10. The reading passage has six paragraphs, A–F. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A–F. NB You may use any letter more than once.
